statement:
The integers \(1, 2, 3, \ldots, 2016\) are written on a board. You may choose any two numbers and replace them with their average. After \(2015\) such replacements, one number remains.

(a) Prove that there is a sequence of replacements making the final number equal to \(2\).

(b) Prove that there is a sequence of replacements making the final number equal to \(1000\).

Consider the system of \(10\) equations in \(10\) real variables \(v_1, \ldots, v_{10}\):
\[v_i = 1 + \frac{6v_i^2}{v_1^2 + v_2^2 + \cdots + v_{10}^2} \qquad (i = 1, \ldots, 10).\]
Find all \(10\)-tuples \((v_1, v_2, \ldots, v_{10})\) that are solutions.
Find all polynomials \(P(x)\) with integer coefficients such that \(P(P(n) + n)\) is a prime number for infinitely many integers \(n\).

Let \(A\), \(B\), and \(F\) be positive integers with \(A < B < 2A\). A flea starts at \(0\) on the number line and may jump right by \(A\) or by \(B\). Lavaman places lava on finitely many intervals of the form \(\{m+1, m+2, \ldots, m+A\}\) (of \(A\) consecutive positive integers), subject to: (i) any two intervals are disjoint and non-adjacent; (ii) at least \(F\) lava-free positive integers lie between any two intervals; (iii) no lava is placed below \(F\). Prove that the smallest \(F\) for which the flea can always avoid the lava is \(F = (n-1)A + B\), where \(n\) is the positive integer satisfying \(\dfrac{A}{n+1} \leq B - A < \dfrac{A}{n}\).

Let \(\triangle ABC\) be an acute-angled triangle with altitudes \(AD\) and \(BE\) meeting at \(H\). Let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(AB\). Suppose the circumcircles of \(\triangle DEM\) and \(\triangle ABH\) meet at points \(P\) and \(Q\), with \(P\) on the same side of \(CH\) as \(A\). Prove that the lines \(ED\), \(PH\), and \(MQ\) all pass through a single point on the circumcircle of \(\triangle ABC\).
